annotation.title_clean: Artificial Intelligence, Automation, and the Economy
annotation.title_en: Artificial Intelligence, Automation, and the Economy
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Executive Office of the President (Council of Economic Advisers, Domestic Policy Council, National Economic Council, OMB, OSTP)
annotation.venue: White House / Executive Office of the President
annotation.summary_en: December 2016 White House report analysing the economic and labor-market effects of AI-driven automation and proposing three policy strategies: invest in and develop AI, educate and train workers, and aid worker transitions to ensure broadly shared growth.
key_provisions_or_claims: AI-driven automation will raise productivity but may disrupt livelihoods and increase inequality absent policy action.
Outcomes depend on institutions and policies, not technology alone.
Strategy 1: invest in and develop AI for its benefits.
Strategy 2: educate and train Americans for future jobs.
Strategy 3: aid workers in transition and empower them to ensure broadly shared growth.
